title: Authenticated checkout return and buyer isolation
goal: Return signed-in marketplace buyers to their own paid order confirmation while preserving guest-token checkout

in: Route authenticated checkout success to buyer-authorized paid order confirmation.
Preserve guest opaque-token order confirmation and add focused branch and denial tests.
out: Making guest tokens guessable or exposing other buyers orders.

acceptance_criteria: Signed-in buyer returns from test checkout to a loadable own-order confirmation.
Guest success still resolves only through opaque guest token.
Wrong signed-in user cannot load another buyers order.
Focused tests cover authenticated and guest success URL branches and authorization.

evidence: Local: 3 focused Jest suites passed, 19 tests including wrong-buyer/unsigned denial, session mismatch, and guest flow.
Full repository typecheck was attempted by the implementation agent but interrupted after about two minutes without diagnostics; no hosted checkout was run.

All marketplace checkout Jest suites passed locally (3 suites, 11 tests); focused checkout/order lint and scoped diff whitespace checks passed. Shared worktree is dirty at HEAD 623b576b7963d4a2eccb2fbf83f24f2011842a83; no Stripe or hosted actor run.
QA-004 product repair validation rerun (2026-09-22): Checkout and buyer order-access Jest: 3 suites, 11 tests passed; signed-in/guest return and wrong-buyer denial remain local proof only.

Criterion status: all four met locally. (1) signed-in buyer returns to a loadable own-order confirmation: met. (2) guest success resolves only through the opaque token: met. (3) wrong signed-in user cannot load another buyer's order: met. (4) focused tests cover both success URL branches and authorization: met.

npx jest --runTestsByPath over the 7 focused marketplace route suites: 7 suites, 25 tests passed. npx vitest run lib/marketplace/__tests__ __tests__/marketplace: 19 files, 186 tests passed. npx eslint on 12 focused marketplace files: exit 0.

progress.summary: Wave 33: all four MKT-005 acceptance criteria remain met locally and were re-verified at 7 suites / 25 marketplace route tests; the authenticated checkout return and buyer isolation contract is unchanged. The staged Stripe test-mode rerun is still open. One concrete hardening was scoped and deliberately not shipped in this lane because it would have silently rewritten this task's own verified test contract.
completed: Authenticated success URL now carries order UUID and Stripe session identifier; guest opaque token path remains.
Order loader verifies signed-in buyer, buyer ownership, and stored session on Stripe return.
Purchase history links to buyer-authorized order confirmation.

Re-verified without product change: the signed-in buyer Stripe return still loads only for a matching stored session, a wrong signed-in buyer is still denied even with the correct session id, an unsigned visitor is still denied, and a guest still resolves only through the opaque 64-character token.
next_steps: Deploy to isolated staging and rerun the authenticated buyer, wrong buyer, guest buyer and seller visibility matrix in Stripe test mode on one exact SHA.

Open recommendation, not shipped: app/marketplace/order/order-access.ts:38 and :61 resolve a signed-in buyer's order through the service-role client with an application-level buyer_user_id filter, so RLS is bypassed on that read. marketplace_orders_participant_read (supabase/migrations/20260410120000_marketplace_core.sql:316) would enforce it server-side. This lane built and then reverted that change because app/api/marketplace/checkout/__tests__/order-access.test.ts:41-85 asserts the current query order and client across five cases, so it needs its own reviewed task rather than riding along in a registry cleanup.
blockers: Live test-mode checkout and the buyer/seller actor matrix require an isolated staging deployment and protected Stripe test configuration, which this lane does not have. No hosted or payment-provider result is claimed.
The buyer-path RLS hardening above was not shipped in this lane; buyer isolation is currently proven by the application filter and its tests, not by a database-enforced policy on that read.
